beats.caption: Cinemory. Your photos, made into a short film
beats.narration: There is always one evening you wish you could keep. Give Cinemory the photos from that night and it hands you back a short film, with music, with titles, and with proof of where every frame came from.

beats.caption: Up to five photos. A limit of this demo, not of the reel maker
beats.narration: This is the real app, live on Cloud Run, and nothing is staged. I drop in five photos from an anniversary dinner. No account, no watermark. Five is the cap so a reel finishes while you watch, and the app says that limit belongs to the demo, not the reel maker.

beats.caption: Six occasions. Each sets the music, pacing and titles
beats.narration: Then I pick the occasion. Each one carries its own music, its own pacing, its own titles, so an anniversary sounds nothing like an award night.

beats.caption: 5 photos, about 6 minutes. All five calls run at once
beats.narration: The app tells you the wait up front, from the photo count. And here is what changed: all five photos go through Genblaze to Kling on GMI Cloud at once, not one behind another. This run packed twenty-five minutes of model work into seven and a half minutes.

beats.caption: The job id is in the link. Reload, and the reel is still there
beats.narration: And you are not stuck on this page while it runs. The job id goes into the link the moment the job is submitted, so I can reload the tab and the reel is still here, still being made. That is what makes it usable.

beats.caption: The reel plays. The people in it are model generated
beats.narration: And there it is. Five photographs, now moving, cut to the music the occasion chose. Everyone you see was made by a model, so nobody real appears in this demo.

beats.caption: Press Verify. Your own browser recomputes the SHA-256
beats.narration: Here is the part that matters most. The provenance panel lists every step, the model, the prompt, and a hash for every asset. I press Verify, and my own browser recomputes the SHA-256 against the sealed manifest. Every check passes, and you can run the same check yourself.

beats.caption: Every artifact in B2, content addressed and indexed
beats.narration: All of it lands in Backblaze B2. Every photo, every clip, the finished reel and the sealed manifest, each under its own content hash. An append-only index catalogues every object, and each job reports what it burned, so a bucket becomes a library.

beats.caption: One core, three ports. Live adapters, offline fakes in CI
beats.narration: This is built to last. One core, three ports, so the live Genblaze and B2 adapters swap for offline fakes and the whole pipeline runs in tests with no credentials. Six hundred tests, contract tested against the real SDK, and security scans on every push.

beats.caption: Live now · open source · github.com/upgradedev/cinemory
beats.narration: Every push to main deploys itself, and it only passes if the live service reports the commit it just built. When the model fails, Cinemory names the reason in plain words instead of leaving you watching a spinner. It began as one gift, for one anniversary. It is live now, open source, and waiting for your photos.
